prior_hypotheses:
- White Matter Microstructural Integrity Mediates Network-Specific Connectivity Disruptions in Insomnia: This hypothesis proposes that white matter microstructural abnormalities in insomnia specifically disrupt connectivity between the salience network and default mode network, independent of global hyperarousal or limbic vulnerability.
- Thalamocortical Coupling Disruption Links Insomnia to Limbic Structural Vulnerability: Disrupted thalamocortical coupling in insomnia may drive limbic structural vulnerability, leading to hippocampal volume reduction and impaired frontolimbic connectivity.
- REM/NREM Switching Dysregulation Impairs Salience-DMN Coupling in Insomnia: Disrupted REM/NREM transitions in insomnia may decouple the salience network from the default mode network, impairing emotional regulation through altered connectivity in prefrontal and cingulate regions.
- Integrated Mechanism of Thalamocortical-White Matter Coupling and REM Disruption in Insomnia: This hypothesis proposes that insomnia arises from a synergistic disruption of thalamocortical coupling, white matter microstructural integrity, and REM/NREM switching, collectively impairing salience-DMN connectivity and limbic structural integrity.
- Adenosine-Driven DMN-Limbic Disconnection in Insomnia Impairs Memory Consolidation: Chronic insomnia disrupts adenosine-mediated synchronization between the default mode network (DMN) and limbic regions, impairing memory consolidation through hyperarousal and structural vulnerability.
